john_acme_ops: Hey team, we started seeing a sharp p99 spike on /v1/generate for tenant acme around 14:03 UTC — p95 ~1.2s -> ~4s, p99 ~3.5s -> ~15s. Also seeing some 502s. Request IDs: req_63a2f, req_63a2f+1. Model: llama-13b-q8, deployment gpu-34. Can you take a look?

sam_support: Sorry about that — escalating. Can you paste one of the 502 responses and a small sample trace? Are you on Hosted or Dedicated?

john_acme_ops: Hosted (dedicated capacity for acme). Sample error: "502 Bad Gateway: upstream reset". Trace link: https://console.redwood/s/trace/req_63a2f. I also attached a short log from our side: 
```
2026-03-10T14:03:12Z ERROR request=req_63a2f worker=gpu-34 code=502 upstream=reset
2026-03-10T14:03:14Z WARN tokenize latency 12ms
2026-03-10T14:03:14Z ERROR runtime: cuda error: out of memory allocating 1536MB
```

sam_support: thanks. tagging runtime + sre. @diego_runtime @nina_sre can you look?

diego_runtime: looking. I can already see a pattern on gpu-34 — repeated OOMs and sustained GPU memory growth correlated with long-tail sessions. KV cache size for tenant acme has grown from ~1.4GB -> ~4.2GB over the last hour (we've been keeping per-tenant caches in-process). Metrics: gpu_mem_usage p95 72% -> 92%, p99 95%+. p95 latency jumped after batch queuing increased. Likely fragmentation + KV growth causing allocator to fail to satisfy contiguous allocations, leading to fallback paths that push latency way up.

nina_sre: immediate mitigations to consider (low-risk first):
- route acme traffic off gpu-34 to a different pool (routing policy)
- temporarily pin acme to smaller model variant (llama-7b-q8) or enable a fallback model at router level
- reduce max_tokens and concurrent requests from their client if possible
- trigger rolling restart for the affected workers to reclaim GPU memory (non-disruptive if we drain first)

sam_support: @john_acme_ops can you do the token/concurrency change on your side? We'll prepare migration + restart plan.

john_acme_ops: I can reduce max_tokens from 4096 -> 1024 and set concurrency limit to 4. Do that now.

diego_runtime: thanks — while that's in-flight, quick config we can flip on the service side to throttle KV growth (low-risk):
```
{"kv_cache": {"enabled": true, "max_entries": 300000, "eviction_policy": "lru", "eviction_threshold": 0.85}}
```
This will start evicting long-tail prefixes and stop unbounded growth. Also enable compact_kv=true for the pool to trigger periodic compaction.

eng_runtime_oncall: I'll run a targeted drain + rolling restart for gpu-34. Plan: set pool read-only, wait 60s to drain in-flight, restart workers one-by-one, verify mem histograms. Command I'll run: `rdwctl pool set-mode gpu-34 drain && rdwctl restart-pool --pool=gpu-34 --grace=60`

nina_sre: also recommend we temporarily change allocator tuning to be more aggressive about freeing small slabs: set `slab_compact_interval=30s` and reduce `slab_slab_size` from 512MiB -> 256MiB for the short term. That cuts worst-case fragmentation.

diego_runtime: we'll also enable the defrag job on the nodes: `kubectl apply -f jobs/redwood-gpu-defrag.yaml -n prod` — it runs the runtime's defrag binary that compacts free blocks.

john_acme_ops: changes applied on our side (tokens + concurrency). We approved fallback to 7b. Please proceed.

sam_support: noted. @eng_runtime_oncall please proceed with the drain and config flips. Keep me posted and I'll update the customer.

eng_runtime_oncall: started drain now. flipping kv_cache eviction to LRU on gpu-34 via feature flag. Running restart command (pods will restart over next ~4m). I'll post mem histograms + p95/p99 after restarts.

diego_runtime: after flip we should see KV growth flatten and OOMs stop. If not, we'll escalate to allocator vendor for a micropatch. Also creating a short-run playbook with exact thresholds for automatic eviction/defrag for the pool.

sam_support: great — john, once we confirm p99 back to normal we'll close. Thanks for quick action. :thumbsup:

john_acme_ops: initial results: p95 down to ~900ms, p99 ~1800ms after routing + restart. No more 502s in the last 6 minutes. Will keep monitoring.

sam_support: awesome — leaving this thread open for 24h monitoring. I'll file a follow-up ticket for a permanent fix (KV limits + allocator tuning) and post-runbook. Ticket: TKT-3421.

deploy-bot: action=restart-pool pool=gpu-34 status=initiated by=eng_runtime_oncall timestamp=2026-03-10T14:06:40Z

sam_support: closing notes: next steps: 1) permanent kv_quota per-tenant, 2) improved eviction heuristics (age+size), 3) automated defrag job cadence, 4) consider switching acme to dedicated smaller model family for cost/latency predictability. I'll drop a short postmortem once we have histograms.

john_acme_ops: thanks everyone, appreciate the quick turnaround.
